subject: Presenting a standard error in relation to a transformed intercept estimate

messages.author: 6b30f83fdab3a4d4
messages.subject: Presenting a standard error in relation to a transformed intercept estimate
parts:
Hello unmarked group,

I writing up a manuscript now that in which the bulk of the analysis was performed using the colext function in unmarked. I'm wondering how I should present the SE error of  transformed intercepts and coefficient estimates. At the bottom of my post is an output of one of the models in our model section set.

I want to present the back transformed extinction estimate from this model, which is plogis(1.79)=0.72. Should I be transforming the SE as well to present along side the transformed intercept estimate plogis(0.573)=0.62? 

If this a reasonable way to present it, the natural thing for a reader to do is look at the SE and multiply it by 1.96 to get a 95% CI, and I know that it is not the correct thing to do. Any other suggestions for presenting uncertainty with regard to transformed intercepts would be greatly appreciated.

colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~1, epsilonformula = ~1, 
    pformula = ~julian + Tmax + Depth, data = umf)

messages.subject: Re: Presenting a standard error in relation to a transformed intercept estimate
parts:
Hi Sean,

Marc and Richard have a nice vignette for that here: Dynamic occupancy models in unmarked

This explains, among other things, how to get confidence intervals for back-transformed estimates.  The SE is only meaningful on the link scale.
